en: Yahya ibn Yahya, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Zuhayr said: "narrated to us," and the other two said: "Jarir informed us"—from al-A'mash, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) never criticized any food at all; if he desired something he ate it, and if he disliked it he left it.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me, Ishaq ibn 'Isa narrated to us, Malik informed us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) entertained a guest who was an unbeliever. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered a sheep for him, and it was milked, and he drank its milk; then another, and he drank it; then another, and he drank it, until he drank the milk of seven sheep. In the morning he embraced Islam. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered a sheep for him, and he drank its milk, then he ordered another, but he could not finish it. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The believer drinks in one intestine, while the unbeliever drinks in seven intestines."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with the like of their hadith.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, Burayd narrated to us, from his grandfather, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "The believer eats in one intestine, while the unbeliever eats in seven intestines."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it, and did not mention Ibn 'Umar.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir and Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The believer eats in one intestine, while the unbeliever eats in seven intestines."

Abu Bakr ibn Khallad al-Bahili narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Waqid ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd that he heard Nafi' say: Ibn 'Umar saw a poor person, so he kept placing food before him and placing food before him. He said: And the man began eating a great deal of food. He said: Thereupon Ibn 'Umar said: "Do not let this man enter upon me again, for indeed I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'The unbeliever eats in seven intestines.'"

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abu Usamah and Ibn Numayr said: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub; both of them from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, they said: Yahya—who is al-Qattan—informed us, from 'Ubaydullah, Nafi' informed me, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "The unbeliever eats in seven intestines, while the believer eats in one intestine."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, they said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "The food of one man suffices two men, the food of two men suffices four, and the food of four suffices eight."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Abu Bakr and Abu Kurayb said: "narrated to us," and the other two said: "Abu Mu'awiyah informed us"—from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The food of one person suffices two, and the food of two suffices four."

Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with the like of the hadith of Ibn Jurayj.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Rawh ibn 'Ubadah informed us; (H) and Yahya ibn Habib narrated to me, Rawh narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "The food of one person suffices two, the food of two suffices four, and the food of four suffices eight." And in the narration of Ishaq: "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said," without mentioning "I heard."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The food of two suffices three, and the food of three suffices four."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, Salim ibn Nuh al-'Attar narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, who said: Guests came to stay with us—he said—and my father used to converse with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) at night. He said: So he went off and said: "O 'Abd al-Rahman, attend to your guests." He said: When evening came, we brought them their hospitality meal—he said—but they refused, saying: "Not until the master of our house comes and eats with us." He said: I said to them: "He is a stern man, and if you do not do so, I fear that harm from him may befall me." He said: But they refused. When he came, he did not begin with anything before asking about them, saying: "Have you attended to your guests?" They said: "No, by Allah, we have not." He said: "Did I not order 'Abd al-Rahman?" He said: And I stepped aside from him, so he called: "O 'Abd al-Rahman!" He said: But I stayed away. He said: Then he said: "O Ghunthar! I adjure you, if you can hear my voice, you must come!" He said: So I came and said: "By Allah, I am not at fault! Here are your guests, so ask them; I brought them their meal, but they refused to eat until you arrived." He said: So Abu Bakr said: "What is the matter with you that you would not accept your hospitality meal from us?" He said: Then Abu Bakr said: "By Allah, I will not eat it tonight!" He said: Thereupon they said: "By Allah, we will not eat it until you eat it!" He said: "I have never seen evil like tonight! Woe to you, what is the matter with you that you do not accept your hospitality meal from us?" He said: Then he said: "As for the first, that was from Satan; bring your meal!" He said: The food was brought, so he mentioned the Name of Allah and ate, and they ate. He said: In the morning, he went to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, they kept their oath while I broke mine." He said: So he told him, whereat the Prophet said: "Rather, you are the most dutiful and best of them." He said: And no expiation reached me.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari, Hamid ibn 'Umar al-Bakrawi, and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la al-Qaysi narrated to us, all from al-Mu'tamir—and the wording is Ibn Mu'adh's—al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: My father said: Abu 'Uthman narrated to us, that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr narrated to him that the people of al-Suffah were poor people, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) once said: "Whoever has food for two, let him take a third person; and whoever has food for four, let him take a fifth or a sixth," or as he said. And Abu Bakr brought three, while the Prophet of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) went with ten, and Abu Bakr with three. He said: There was he, I, my father, and my mother—and I do not know if he also said: and my wife, and a servant between our house and Abu Bakr's house. He said: Abu Bakr had dinner with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), then stayed until the 'Isha' prayer was performed; then he returned and stayed until the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) became drowsy, and came home after as much of the night had passed as Allah willed. His wife said to him: "What kept you away from your guests?"—or she said: "from your guest?" He said: "Have you not served them dinner?" She said: "They refused until you come; they offered it to them, but they insisted on waiting." He said: So I went and hid myself, and he said: "O Ghunthar!" and he scolded and cursed, saying: "Eat, may it not be wholesome!" and said: "By Allah, I will never eat of it!" He said: By Allah, we did not take a morsel except that from underneath it there grew more than it, until we were satisfied, and it became more than it had been before. Abu Bakr looked at it and behold, it was as it was or even more! He said to his wife: "O sister of Banu Firas, what is this?" She said: "No, by the delight of my eye, it is now three times more than it was before!" He said: So Abu Bakr ate from it and said: "That was only from Satan"—meaning his oath—then he ate a morsel from it, then carried it to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and it remained with him by morning. He said: There was a covenant between us and a people, and the term had expired; so we appointed twelve men as leaders, and with each man of them were people—Allah knows best how many were with each man—except that he sent with them, and all of them ate from it, or as he said.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari, Hamid ibn 'Umar al-Bakrawi, and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, all from al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman—and the wording is Ibn Mu'adh's—al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman—and he also narrated—from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, who said: We were one hundred and thirty with the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Does any one of you have food?" Behold, there was a man with a sa' of food or something similar, and it was kneaded. Then a tall pagan man with disheveled hair arrived driving some sheep. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Is it for sale, or a gift?"—or he said: "or a present?" He said: "No, rather for sale." So he bought a sheep from him, and it was prepared, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) ordered that its liver and stomach contents (sawad al-batn) be roasted. He said: By Allah, there was not one among the one hundred and thirty except that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) cut off a piece for him from its liver: if he was present, he gave it to him, and if he was absent, he saved it for him. He said: And he made two large bowls; so all of us ate from them and were satisfied, and there remained food in the two bowls, which I loaded onto the camel, or as he said.
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, with this chain of narration.
